Title: What does 'time-based cache charge' mean per provider?
What is open (description): How Joaa's statement ('Normal cached tokens cost 1/10 of normal input tokens ... cache is also billing how long you are keeping the cache normally 1/10 of input token for an hour', S-J-001) maps onto each provider's pricing. Stored pages show: Anthropic and OpenAI price cache writes and reads (with cache lifetimes of minutes to 24 hours); Gemini explicit caching adds an hourly storage price.
What is known now: Time-based cache charges per provider, from the stored dated vendor pages (retrieved 2026-10-11): Anthropic default 5-minute lifetime; a 1-hour TTL at 2x the base input price, set via cache_control ttl '1h'; the automatic server-tool-result breakpoint always uses the 5-minute TTL (EXT-0085, EXT-0152, EXT-0158); Bedrock TTL 5 minutes on many models, reset on each hit (EXT-0137); OpenAI cache writes 1.25x with reads 0.1x, GPT-5.6 and later 30m TTL, earlier models in_memory (about 5-10 minutes, up to an hour) or 24h (EXT-0086, EXT-0142); Gemini explicit caching adds an hourly storage price, $0.50 per million tokens per hour through 2026 and $1.00 from 2027-01-01, from the pricing page only (EXT-0089). Joaa's 'normally 1/10 of input token for an hour' matches the Gemini pricing page and the 0.1x read multiplier on older Anthropic/OpenAI models; other models and providers differ (0.05x, 0.025x on newer ones, EXT-0085).
